criteria.rationale: For a consumer travel service the defining risk is contribution margin per booking and repeat. The founders candidly list manual operations, partner quality and seasonality as risks, but give no plan. Paid CAC (~INR 640) eats over half the ~INR 1,130 commission per booking before operations cost. The deck also inflates the customer facts: 'thousands of travellers' against ~1,300, operations in two states and 'growing across India' against Jaipur only, and 'planned by AI' against templates confirmed manually. These contradictions count against candour.

Paid acquisition ~INR 640 per booking; revenue INR 4.6 L on 410 bookings (~INR 1,130 each).
Founder-listed key risks: partner quality, seasonality, manual operations that do not yet scale.

gates.detail: Checked against all 88 portfolio companies. Hotelzify (Shopify for small hotels) sells software to hotels; Yatrika would book stays, not compete. DevDham (temples online for devotees) and Vivahit (wedding management) reach families on adjacent occasions, but neither assembles or books holiday trips. SuperLiving (family lifestyle app) and the consumer-tech names (Knot, Cherry, Spill Games, Plazza, NPrep) do unrelated jobs. No same customer + same job. C003 was shown but does not apply.
No dependence on a regulatory permission; travel booking on commission needs no new rule.

case_for: Real problem-specific experience: ten years running a family travel agency, and the startup operates trips hands-on (R2, S3).
Some paying demand and early repeat: 410 bookings, INR 38.6 L GBV, 14% of families booking again (R3).
Small ask the fund could lead (S2).
case_against: The deck overstates traction and reach ('thousands of travellers', two states, 'across India') against ~1,300 travellers from Jaipur in the form (R1).
Thin unit economics: paid CAC takes over half the commission per booking before manual operations cost, and no contribution margin is given (R1, R3).
The 'AI' is an LLM over templates while MakeMyTrip and others give AI itineraries away free; this is essentially an agency (R6, G3).
Crowded category, with Thrillophilia headquartered in the same city and no competitors named (R4, S4).
call_questions: Your deck says 'thousands of travellers across Rajasthan and Uttarakhand'; the form says ~1,300 from Jaipur. Which is right, and why does the deck read differently?
Of the 410 bookings, how many came from your family agency's past customers, how many from Instagram and how many from paid ads? Is the agency still trading separately?
What does a booking cost you in staff time, calls and refunds, and what is contribution margin after CAC?
Why would a Tier-2 family book with you rather than use MakeMyTrip's free AI planner or a local agent?
What milestones does INR 1.2 Cr get you to, and over how many months?
What is the name and GSTIN of the family agency, and can we speak to three repeat families?
what_would_change_our_view: Positive contribution margin per booking after CAC and operations, repeat measured on cohorts not drawn from the family agency, and traction claims that match across deck and form would let us look again.
